service.name: Live music for a holiday party at home
service.serviceType: A Christmas party band, a Christmas jazz duo or trio, live band karaoke or a DJ for holiday parties at home, Thanksgiving week dinners and New Year's Eve at a house
service.description: Live music for a holiday party at home across Denver and the Front Range: a Christmas jazz duo or trio playing the season and the standards at 65 to 72 dBA, a singer with a guitar, a party band for the floor, live band karaoke for a big main floor, and a DJ through the same sound system on the same contract, with sound support sized to the house and one personal contact for the night.

faqs.q: Can we book a band for a Christmas party at home?
faqs.a: Yes. A house books four sizes in December: one guitarist or a singer with a guitar for an open house or a dinner, the Christmas jazz duo or trio for drinks and dinner at a volume the table talks across, a party band (a trio or quartet, or live band karaoke on a big main floor) for the part of the night when the furniture moves, and a DJ on their own or after the band through the same sound system. It's one contract with one personal contact, and sound support that's the right size for the house is included.

faqs.q: What does live music for a holiday party at home cost?
faqs.a: What live music costs in this market is set out on our pricing page, and the cost guide has the Colorado figures for each kind of night, house parties included. December is the season where the peak weekends carry their own line on the quote, so send the date with the enquiry and we'll come back with a configuration and a price for that night rather than a range.

faqs.q: Do you play Christmas music, or just the standards?
faqs.a: Both, and the balance is yours to set. The Christmas jazz trio draws on three books: the Vince Guaraldi record from the Charlie Brown special, the standards that are Christmas songs (White Christmas, The Christmas Song, Let It Snow, Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas), and the standards that aren't, threaded through so a three-hour party doesn't hear the same twelve carols four times. Some houses want carols wall to wall and some want one Christmas set placed where the evening wants it.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book a December Saturday?
faqs.a: As soon as you have the date. In 2026 the December Saturdays before Christmas are the 5th, the 12th and the 19th, every office party in the city wants the same three nights, and those bookings get decided between August and October. A weeknight or a Sunday in December is an easier ask, and a party in January is the easiest of all.

faqs.q: Can the same band play dinner and then the party?
faqs.a: Yes. A duo plays drinks and dinner at 65 to 72 dBA at the nearest table and the same booking grows to a trio or a quartet for the floor, and the DJ can carry the late end of the night through the same sound system on the same contract. Tejas Singh is the act we recommend first for a night built that way: one voice through dinner, a quartet for the dancing.

faqs.q: Do you play Thanksgiving or Friendsgiving?
faqs.a: Yes. Thanksgiving is Thursday, November 26 in 2026, and the week books two ways: the night before, when the house is full of people who flew in, and the Friendsgiving on the Saturday before or after. Both are dinners, so both book a solo or a duo playing the standards at conversation volume, with the season kept out of the set unless you ask for it. Christmas Eve and Christmas Day dinners book the same size.

faqs.q: Can you play New Year's Eve at a house?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's the date to send first, because New Year's Eve (a Thursday in 2026) gets booked earlier than any other night of the season. At home it's a trio or a quartet with the DJ through the same sound system, the countdown gets the announcement microphone, and the night stays indoors because it runs late.

faqs.q: How much space does the band need in a house?
faqs.a: A solo or a DJ takes 6 by 4 feet, a duo 8 by 6, a trio 12 by 8 and a quartet 14 by 10, each on one dedicated circuit (the quartet and the live band karaoke four-piece want two), a circuit the oven and the coffee makers aren't on. Load-in runs 45 minutes for a solo or a DJ and an hour for a duo or a trio, and the tree usually stands in the corner the band would take, so tell us which corner is ours. Footprints for every size are on the technical page.

faqs.q: Is a small holiday party too small for live music?
faqs.a: No. A dinner for twelve books one guitarist or a singer with a guitar, which sets up in 6 by 4 feet on one circuit and plays at a volume the table talks across, and an open house books a duo that works whether twelve or sixty people are in the house at the time. The size that turns a holiday party at home is usually smaller than the host imagines.
